title: Git fixture tests fail when the runner's environment sets GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL
outcome: Observed on Windows B, S0 FULL test-4f73bcbb-7a69-40b6-a40d-2c79c4ec03eb (commit bd01930c, 2026-11-22 02:17-02:59Z). The runner carried GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https from its fetch isolation into the launcher's test child. Git treats that variable as protocol.allow=never plus an explicit allow-list that overrides protocol.<name>.allow config, so the suite's own `-c protocol.file.allow=always` no longer permits local fixture transport. 13 Rust tests failed, all with "fatal: transport 'file' not allowed": submodule, push and sync fixtures in tests::git, tests::acceptance_evaluation::sighting::committed_input, tests::test_runs::engram_verification_record::declared and tests::test_runs::test_run_registration::clone_binding. The same commit passed its Linux FULL test-5db67132 without the variable. Primary cause: the runner's invocation (classified runner/environment). This item covers the test side: the fixtures' git child processes already pin protocol.file.allow, but they inherit GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, so a runner environment that has really occurred defeats them.
acceptance: The Rust test suite's local Git fixtures run with the permissions they declare, whatever GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL the parent environment sets, without allowing any transport beyond local file transport.
A test run with GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https set in the launching environment passes the tests that failed on Windows B in test-4f73bcbb.
